mappings.name: kill9: a confirm whose status query is slow, selected by MSISDN rather than by reference

why: THE ENTRY POINT of the only status query an end-to-end confirm can make slow.
requesttopay-status.json's ...0560 mapping already answers slowly, but it is keyed
on a fixed reference and a confirm cannot choose its reference (the handler mints
provider_reference_id with Uuid::new_v4() before committing the charge, and a seam
to fix it from a test would be a code path that exists only outside production --
AGENTS.md's first rule). MTN's status query is a GET carrying no body, so the
steering has to happen HERE, on the POST, and be carried forward by scenario state
-- the same technique, and the same documentation-MSISDN block, as
requesttopay-scenario.json's `mtn-e2e-poll`.
237600000ce9 continues that file's 0ce0 convention; the trailing 9 names the signal
worker_kill9.rs sends (SIGKILL).
Answers a plain 202 because this mapping exists to MOVE THE SCENARIO, not to change
what a confirm sees: the crash under test is the WORKER's, and up to the point the
worker polls, this confirm must be indistinguishable from any other.

mappings.name: kill9: the first status query takes thirty seconds, whatever the reference

why: Thirty seconds is chosen against vpay_provider::DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT (20 s), not
against a stopwatch: it is longer, so this request CANNOT be answered before the
worker's own deadline fires. A test that killed the worker a little late therefore
still cannot settle the charge behind the assertion's back -- it fails loudly
instead, which is the failure mode worker_kill9.rs wants from a slow machine.
newScenarioState fires when the stub MATCHES the request, not when it finishes
answering it (verified against wiremock/wiremock:3.9.2 before this file was
written: during a 30 s delay, GET /__admin/scenarios already reports the new state
and POST /__admin/requests/count already counts the request). That is what makes
the SIGKILLed poll observable at all, and what makes the SECOND worker's poll --
the one that must settle the charge -- fast.
Matches ANY reference, so it is usable from a real confirm. Three things keep it
from swallowing an unrelated case, exactly as for `mtn-e2e-poll`:
1. requiredScenarioState -- only the POST above leaves `Started`, and no other
suite, and no demo, sends that MSISDN;
2. priority 4 is below the reference-keyed status mappings (priority 1), so
...0404, ...0f01 and the rest keep winning even inside this scenario;
3. priority 4 is above `mtn-e2e-poll`'s priority-5 status mappings, so a
container that somehow had both scenarios armed would answer deterministically
rather than by mapping insertion order. No suite arms both: each test starts
its own container.

mappings.name: kill9: every later status query answers SUCCESSFUL at once

why: No newScenarioState, so the scenario rests here and every later poll answers the
same thing -- which is what makes 'the charge settles EXACTLY once' a real
assertion rather than an artefact of the stub changing its mind.
financialTransactionId is distinct from both 1234567891 (the reference-keyed
scenario) and e2e-1234567892 (mtn-e2e-poll), so an assertion on
charges.provider_txn_id cannot pass by reading another stub's answer.

mappings.name: kill9: a submit that takes thirty seconds to answer, selected by MSISDN

why: docs/flows/crash-safety.md's kill point 2 -- 'POST issued, response lost' -- staged
against the SHIPPING vpay-server rather than written into the database.
worker_kill9.rs confirms with this MSISDN, waits until the charge is committed in
`submitting` with an unanswered provider_requests row (write first, network
second), and SIGKILLs the server while this delay is still running. The response
never reaches anyone, which is precisely what 'the answer was lost' means.
No scenario: nothing about the recovery depends on a second POST. The recovery
table's answer for an unanswered submit is POLL, and the poll falls through to
requesttopay-status.json's catch-all SUCCESSFUL (priority 10) like any other
reference -- so a resubmit, which would show up as a second POST in the journal,
is something that test can assert did NOT happen.
